\section{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Moments}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Moments
\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Moments: Introduction}
Multilinear monomials in independent centered inputs of unit second moment are orthonormal. Their coefficient identities give means, second moments, and invariance under changing unused inputs.

\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $(X_i)_{i\in
I}$ be mutually independent real random variables in $L^2$, each with mean zero and
second moment one. For subsets $S,T\subseteq I$, $\mathbb E\big[(\prod_{i\in
S}X_i)(\prod_{i\in T}X_i)\big]$ equals $1$ if $S=T$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourth integrability of monomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.monomial_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.monomial_memLp_nat}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let
$X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables in $L^4$. For every
subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the monomial $\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ belongs to $L^4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Inner product of polynomial evaluations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_eval_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_monomial_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.monomial_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{

}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let
$X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables with finite fourth
moments, mean zero, and second moment one. For coefficient families $F,G: \mathcal
P(\{0,\ldots,n-1\})\to\mathbb R$, define $F(X)=\sum_S F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ and
likewise $G(X)$. Then $\mathbb E[F(X)G(X)]=\sum_S F(S)G(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment from squared coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_eval_sq}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each in $L^4$, centered, and with second moment $1$. For $F(X)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ with real coefficients, $\E[F(X)^2]=\sum_S F(S)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean equals the constant coefficient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_eval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.integral_eval_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p026-b007
}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each in $L^4$, centered, and with second moment $1$. For arbitrary real coefficients $F(S)$, $\E[\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i]=F(\varnothing)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation on a Supported Coordinate Set]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.eval_supported}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ assign a real coefficient to every subset of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $X_j:\Omega\to\bbr$ be real-valued functions. For a subset
$s$ of the coordinate set, suppose $F(T)=0$ whenever $T$ is not contained in $s$. Then,
for every $\omega\in\Omega$, the multilinear evaluation
$\sum_{T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)$ equals
$\sum_{T\subseteq s}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation Is Unchanged by an Unused Coordinate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.eval_eq_of_off_coordinate}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ assign a real coefficient to each subset of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $X_j,Y_j:\Omega\to\bbr$ be two families of real-valued
functions. If $F(S)=0$ for every subset $S$ containing a fixed coordinate $i$, and
$X_j=Y_j$ for every $j\ne i$, then the multilinear evaluations of $F$ on the two
families are equal as functions on $\Omega$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection*{Hypercontractivity --- Random Variables --- Moments: Further results}

\begin{theorem}[Finite integrability of monomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.monomial_memLp_nat}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.monomial_memLp_nat}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp_nat}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $p$ be a positive integer, and let $(\Omega,\mu)$
be a probability space. If $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are mutually independent real random
variables in $L^p$, then for every subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ the monomial
$\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ belongs to $L^p$.
\end{theorem}
